headline: ML-derived transcriptomic signatures prioritize prognostic biomarkers in diverse cancers
label: Ml Prognostic Biomarker Signatures
summary: Public cohorts and single-cell data now feed feature-selection ML pipelines that nominate candidate prognostic and immunotherapy biomarkers.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of candidate transcriptomic and multi-omic biomarkers from public resources such as TCGA, GEO, and UK Biobank, using feature-selection and machine-learning pipelines including LASSO-Cox, WGCNA, Boruta, XGBoost, and Random Survival Forest. Several studies integrate single-cell RNA-seq with bulk cohorts to define cell-state programs, such as an IFI27-centered interferon-response epithelial state in bladder cancer. Validation depth varies: a senescence-based melanoma model was screened across 101 ML strategies and tested in six GEO cohorts, while a 9-gene LASSO-Cox hypopharyngeal signature was validated in bulk data. The most extensive integration is an XGBoost model combining plasma proteomics and polygenic risk scores for lung cancer risk (C-statistic 0.803, UK Biobank). Evidentiary weight is uneven and most findings remain candidate-generating rather than mechanistic.
